Voting is taught through citizenship, age, both residence minimums, registration, legal disqualification, and prohibited tests. Ballot secrecy and independent voting are connected to private choice and protection from interference.

The election route is limited to the constitutional pre-1973 group; majority rules are qualified by the applicable historical law. Naturalization ages and residence periods are separated by legal process, with other qualifications explicitly retained.

Marriage protection has the legal-renunciation exception. RA 9225 is limited to natural-born Filipinos and foreign naturalization, with candidacy subject to a separate renunciation and other office qualifications.

Voting thresholds are minimums measured on election day. Registration and legal disqualifications remain necessary. Overseas voting is expressly subject to statutory rules, and independent voting includes the constitutional interim arrangement.
